title: Featured Projects
description: A selection of projects that showcase problem-solving abilities, technical depth, and architectural thinking.

projects.title: TACO
projects.description: Multi-module SaaS platform for commission management across insurance agencies and brokers, built as a modular monolith with a FastAPI backend and Next.js frontend
projects.problem: Insurance agencies and brokers spend excessive time on manual commission tracking and reporting. Existing tools lack the audit trails, role-aware access, and automated reconciliation needed to manage complex carrier statement ingestion and agent payout workflows at scale.
projects.solution: Built TACO as a monorepo with three independently deployable services — a FastAPI backend, an ARQ worker runtime, and a Next.js frontend — each with its own Docker image shipped through GitHub Actions CI/CD and routed in production by Traefik. The backend is a modular monolith organized around ten isolated business modules (auth, tenants, billing, carriers, ingestion, agents, commissions, policies, CRM, notifications), each owning its domain, application, and port layers through hexagonal architecture and CQRS. A manifest-driven platform registry assembles API routes, worker commands, and scheduler jobs at runtime without centralizing that knowledge. Signed command envelopes over a Redis-backed ARQ queue power async statement processing and billing workflows, while Auth0, Stripe, SendGrid, AWS S3/KMS, and Vault handle identity, subscriptions, notifications, file storage, and secrets.
challenges: Designing a manifest-driven composition model so each module registers its own API routes, worker commands, and scheduler jobs without centralizing that knowledge in a monolithic router or task file

Enforcing hexagonal architecture boundaries across ten business modules — keeping domain code free of infrastructure imports and preventing cross-module reach-through during an active migration from legacy HTTP patterns

Building a signed-command worker runtime with versioned payloads, TTL validation, signature verification, deduplication, and dead-letter handling so async ingestion and billing jobs are safe to retry and traceable on failure

Coordinating three independent production runtimes (API, worker, scheduler) so worker contracts, signed-command TTLs, and outbox relay state stay consistent across deployments without requiring simultaneous cutover

projects.title: AudioBookSync
projects.description: Seamless audiobook synchronization platform for Audible users
projects.problem: Users struggle with not actually owning the books they purchase on Audible, leading to issues when switching devices or platforms.
projects.solution: Developed a cloud-based sync system that allows users to upload their Audible audiobooks and sync playback progress across multiple devices.
challenges: Syncing audio playback timestamps across devices accurately
Handling offline scenarios with eventual consistency
Optimizing cloud storage for media metadata

projects.title: ClubCRM
projects.description: Full-stack club management platform with role-aware admin workflows and a modular monolith backend
projects.problem: Student organizations and club operators need one system to manage membership, join requests, events, announcements, and access control without scattering workflows across forms, spreadsheets, and disconnected admin tools.
projects.solution: Built ClubCRM as a modular monolith with a Next.js frontend and FastAPI backend. Each datastore has a deliberate responsibility: PostgreSQL as the system of record for clubs, members, events, and audit logs; MongoDB for flexible join-request documents; Redis for auth sessions and dashboard cache with short TTLs; and Kafka as a prepared async event boundary. Auth is backend-owned, resolving external provider sessions against internal grants and distinguishing authenticated from authorized users across org-admin and club-manager roles.
challenges: Dividing data across four databases without overlap — keeping PostgreSQL for relational correctness, MongoDB for flexible form payloads, Redis for disposable cache and session state, and Kafka as a future-ready async boundary
Managing frontend and backend drift as the UI surface moved faster than the API contract, requiring a gradual migration from placeholder view-model logic to live backend routes
Keeping local development reliable across six services by standardizing on the devcontainer with auto-generated host-port mappings and Docker Compose orchestration

projects.title: ClubCRM Monitoring Stack
projects.description: Off-cluster observability dashboard for a live Kubernetes networking and failover demo
projects.problem: The networking demo needed to stay observable from outside the cluster while nodes, pods, and Longhorn-backed workloads were intentionally disrupted, which meant the observability surface had to survive the same failures it was watching.
projects.solution: Built a standalone off-cluster stack — a FastAPI backend and Next.js dashboard deployed on a separate Hostinger VPS — that watches Kubernetes nodes, pods, and Longhorn volumes via the official Kubernetes client and streams live state to browsers over WebSockets. A lightweight nginx proxy keeps the dashboard on a single origin. The stack also supports snapshot fixture mode for UI rehearsals when live cluster access is unavailable.
challenges: Keeping the monitoring surface completely off-cluster so intentional node and pod disruptions during the demo could not take the dashboard down with it
Normalizing Kubernetes node state, pod placement, Longhorn volume health, and HTTP probe results into a single unified real-time snapshot stream
Supporting both live kubeconfig mode and snapshot fixture mode so the dashboard could be developed and rehearsed before cluster access was available

projects.title: Home Lab Infrastructure
projects.description: Self-hosted infrastructure with Proxmox, Docker, and networking
projects.problem: Need for a scalable, self-hosted infrastructure to run multiple services while maintaining security, monitoring, and ease of deployment.
projects.solution: Built a complete home lab environment using Proxmox for virtualization, Docker for containerization, and Traefik for intelligent routing and reverse proxying.
challenges: Setting up secure networking with proper firewall rules
Managing SSL certificates and automatic renewal
Implementing proper monitoring and alerting systems
